answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than identity count. A sybil cluster may grow like a vine or hide behind an onyx façade, but if few attestations bridge it to honest nodes, its external cut has low conductance. Under bounded-degree and seed-trust assumptions, conductance and min-cut bounds limit the cluster’s reachable trust mass and thus its aggregate voting weight.
